title: The Shelter Line
summary: Rill's cracked horizon cell held its bearing all the way home, and it points at an erosion cave under the ridge foot — where a Driftline courier has been sleeping rough, talking to a wall, and reciting numbers in her sleep. Walk her home along the old shelter line. Slow. Close. Before the season notices she's missing from it.

objectives.label: Follow the cell's bearing to the erosion cave at the ridge foot
Walk Rill's wagon home along the shelter line — stay close
Get Rill inside, off the wind

offer.text: Kid. The cell's bearing cross-checks with the last line in Rill's logbook: *'cave under the foot, the good one, the singing one.'* She went to ground before the wall took the ridge. She's been down there four days.
Four days in a cave in storm season. What shape is she in, Ketch?

Radio pinged her suit beacon at dawn. It's broadcasting on the old band, and under the beeps there's… talking. Steady, rhythmic, mostly numbers. Kid, you bring her home *slow*. Her wagon's still got legs — vane walkers, low gear. You keep pace beside her like the old shelter-line runs, and you do not let the season find a gap between you and her.
One more thing. Whatever she's saying — write it down. All of it. Even the parts that aren't numbers.

accept.text: Station — Pem, on nine. I have been listening to your missing courier's beacon for four days. What he is reciting is not weather and it is not madness. It is an *address*. Knock gently when you arrive. She is mid-conversation.
Copy. Ridge foot, south cave, one sleeping courier, conversational walls. Ridge foot by noon.
Flat salt and a following wind, kid. Bring my idiot home.

complete.text: …four-one-seven, mark, the door stands where the dunes agree, four-one-*seven*, keep the amber on the left shoulder and the — oh. Hello, Ash. You're the new one. Ketch owes me money.
I owe you a *funeral suit*, you vein of rust — four days! Four days I rehearsed the eulogy, Rill, and it was *complimentary*— get in the garage, off the wind, before I miscount my blessings.
Did I do the numbers out loud? I do them in my sleep now. Four-one-seven, mark… Ash. Your crate is a key, you know. The cave told me. The cave is a *very good listener*.

Ketch. I wrote down everything she said on the wagon — and every number she gave me is *lit up* on my map grid. All of them, same spot, past the far glass hills. There's a door out there, and Rill just slept-talked us its address.

…Pin it. Copy it, seal it, and nobody rides that grid alone. Storm season's got half a season left in it, and now it's got a *destination*. Sleep first, kid. The end of the world can hold for one night.
